---
title: "Fatigue damage"
---

Aeolian vibration bends the conductor at the clamp and breaks its outer
strands by fatigue. [](`dohl.damage`) turns a vibration amplitude into a
stress, and a stress into a number of cycles to failure.

## Fictive stress

[](`~dohl.damage.fictive_stress`) computes the bending stress of the outer
strand at the clamp (EPRI Orange Book, chapter "Fatigue of overhead
conductors"), with one of three methods:

- `fymax`: from the antinode amplitude and frequency (eq. 3.2-14);
- `ba_cigre` and `ba_pfs`: from the bending amplitude $Y_b$ at
  $x_b = 89$ mm from the clamp (Poffenberger-Swart, eq. 3.2-15), $Y_b$ being
  derived from $y_{max}$ with the CIGRE formula or the Poffenberger-Swart one.

The stress depends on the last-strand diameter, the Young modulus and the
bending stiffness $EI$; [](`dohl.lifespan`) chooses $EI$ between `EImin`,
`EImax` and their mean with its `fsba` argument.

## Safe border line

[](`~dohl.damage.safe_border_line`) gives the stress amplitude a conductor
withstands for $N$ cycles, for single and multi-layer ACSR (Orange Book,
"Safe Border Line Method"); [](`~dohl.damage.inv_safe_border_line`) gives the
number of cycles for a stress.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from dohl import damage

N = np.logspace(5, 10, 101)
plt.semilogx(N, damage.safe_border_line(N, False), label="single-layer ACSR")
plt.semilogx(N, damage.safe_border_line(N, True), label="multi-layer ACSR")
plt.xlabel("number of cycles")
plt.ylabel("stress amplitude (MPa)")
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```

The [safe border line example](examples/safe_border_line.qmd) compares both
curves with the EPRI fatigue tests.

## Quantile regression

[](`~dohl.damage.num_cycles_qreg_said`) estimates the number of cycles to
failure from reduced tension, amplitude, catenary offset and fictive stress,
by quantile regression on the fatigue tests shipped with the package (Said,
*Metamodel applied to fatigue damage in overhead lines conductors*, CIGRE
2022). It returns the estimates of the `q` and `1 - q` quantiles.
